items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Some of the promoters like George Wein and others.

ctx.x: Real quick. Are there any other venues on the way up for the young lions? Places for them to play, things for them to do, that authenticates the music and makes the music one with the culture. And if so, if not, what can be instituted?

Well that is a good one. There are different ways of getting your education, your musical education from the way I did starting out playing just in dance groups and dance bands and after-hour joints where you play a club that you couldn’t buy liquor by the drink it was illegal and you’d have to go and then everybody would fall by at midnight, 1:00 in the morning, 2:00 and jam sessions. But there’s a lot of different opportunities out now for a lot of the like you say “young lions.” Some of these jazz parties.…

and then I graduated from college and I got married and I got the job and boy I sure am sorry I stopped.” I say, “I’m sorry you stopped, too, but don’t bitch to me about your stopping.” “I got out of college, I got a job, I got a family, so that’s why I had to quit playing.” “Oh, no, you don’t have to quit playing.” You see a whole lot of people out there who didn’t quit playing either. So you just — and it is tough, it is tough. You have to stick in this business, ‘cause it will kill you, it will just waste you…
